tools.title: Bitbucket
tools.summary: Git hosting and code review integrated with Jira.

servers.name: Atlassian Rovo MCP Server
servers.capabilities: Scoped read and write on Bitbucket Cloud workspaces and repositories (permission groups read_bitbucket, write_bitbucket).

tools.notes: Bitbucket Cloud only, and only for workspaces linked to an Atlassian organization. Earlier Atlassian posts said Bitbucket tools needed an API token; the current README lists OAuth 2.1 and API token for Bitbucket.

tools.title: GitHub
tools.summary: Git hosting with pull requests, issues and Actions CI.

servers.name: GitHub MCP Server (remote)
servers.capabilities: Repositories, code, issues, pull requests, Actions and security alerts, with toolsets to restrict exposed tools.

access.consent: Authorize the OAuth app or use a repository-scoped GitHub token
scopes: Depends on the active toolsets and GitHub credential

servers.name: GitHub MCP Server (local, Docker)
servers.capabilities: Same tools as the remote server; GITHUB_HOST targets GitHub Enterprise Server or ghe.com, GITHUB_TOOLSETS limits tools.

access.consent: Provide a GitHub personal access token
scopes: Depends on the active toolsets and token permissions

tools.notes: Remote server is available on all GitHub plans, OAuth by default or a PAT as Bearer header. Use the local Docker server for GitHub Enterprise Server (set GITHUB_HOST).

tools.title: GitLab
tools.summary: DevSecOps platform with Git hosting, merge requests and CI/CD.

servers.name: GitLab MCP server
servers.capabilities: Issues, merge requests, pipelines and project data of the GitLab instance, with the user's permissions.

tools.notes: Self-Managed and Dedicated use https://<your-instance>/api/v4/mcp. GA since GitLab 19.5 on Free, Premium and Ultimate; the server must be allowed for the top-level group (GitLab.com) or the instance. Auth is an OAuth token with the mcp scope or a fine-grained PAT; legacy access tokens get 403. stdio-only clients use npx -y mcp-remote <url>.
